songs.name: Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) Jam

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set with blazing Viola Lee Blues and Midnight Hour
ai_show_review.blurb: The set showcases an explosive Viola Lee Blues jam and a soaring In The Midnight Hour, with Alligator delivering gritty blues power. Jerry's guitar work is transcendent while Phil anchors the improvisations. Overall a high‑energy early‑67 performance captured on decent soundboard sources.
ai_show_review.review: September 3, 1967 at Rio Nido’s Dance Hall finds the Dead in full teenage‑rock stride, firing off an eleven‑song first set that crackles with raw momentum. The show erupts with a monster Viola Lee Blues that rolls into a loose Caution jam before returning to the blues theme, highlighting Pigpen’s gritty organ and harmonica while Garcia weaves soulful leads. A thunderous Alligator follows, its swampy riff work driven by Phil’s steady bass foundation, and the night culminates in an extended In The Midnight Hour where Garcia’s “seeds of a thousand bloomfields” guitar lines soar above a pounding rhythm section. Though Dancin' In The Street stumbles a bit rhythmically, it adds a pop‑flavored contrast that keeps the flow lively. All three soundboard recordings capture the performance with varying degrees of hiss and tape wear, but the Backus SBD (gd67-09-03.sbd.backus.17272.sbeok.shnf) delivers the clearest picture of this high‑energy snapshot from the Dead’s formative year.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard capture that balances clarity with the show’s natural crunch, preserving the energy of the performance while keeping most sections listenable.

key_highlights: Explosive Viola Lee Blues jam with Pigpen’s raw organ and harmonica.
Soaring In The Midnight Hour featuring Garcia’s transcendent lead work.
Gritty Alligator blues romp anchored by Phil’s solid bass.
High‑energy first set despite some tape hiss; captures the band’s rapid evolution.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers transcendent, blues‑laden leads throughout, especially on Viola Lee Blues and the extended Midnight Hour where his interplay between left‑hand rhythm and right‑hand leads shines.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass underpins the long jams with a warm, supportive tone; he later recalled this as one of his best early performances, particularly on Midnight Hour.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s vocals are described as “velvet tongues,” adding presence to the mix, though his rhythm on Dancin' In The Street is noted as loosely timed.
band_performance.Billy: Bill Kreutzmann provides a steady, driving pulse that keeps the set grounded despite occasional tape glitches.
